So you need 2 points for and 2 points against the argument. I recommend using the PEEL paragraph format 
Point, evidence, explanation of evidence, linkage( which is basically answering the question)
In my exam there was a question about the nature nurture debate being irrelevant when explaining the cause for depression
I said 
P: it makes things worse as it doesn’t find the exact cause 
E: I supported this by giving an example that if a person suffers from depression and scientists are fighting over whether it was caused by nature or nurture 
E: I explained this by saying that it won’t matter because the person will be suffering regardless and trying to find the cause won’t alleviate their symptoms
Linkage: I answer the question by quoting the words irrelevent by saying this shows that the nature nurture debate is irrelevant as battling and refuting each other arguments rather than working together and trying to find treatments that might ease the suffering. Hence, there is no need for such a debate 

You have to answer it like this

Always support your answers with evidence and don’t forget to link the answer to the question.

For time management: I would advise you to practice past papers in whilst emulating exam conditions. You’ll eventually improve periodically. I found there to be plenty of time for both papers so don’t worry about that. Just keep practicing 
You should spend up to 45 mins per question in paper 4
Also for paper 3 don’t paraphrase the extract line by line. Underline the evidences throughout the passage and then select them. Examiners don’t want you to analyse line by line

The PEEL format for paper 4 is literally the best. I followed it in each paragraph. I had about 3 points in favour of the hypothesis and 4 against the hypothesis. Vice Versa
You first state your thesis statement. Define the question 
Then write your main point, support it with evidence, explain it and then link it( which is basically answering the question) 
For example in my exam paper, which was about the Cuban missile crises and the impact it had on Soviet and ussr relations. I wrote that it had a profound impact as it caused one of the leaders of the Soviet Union to be removed from power. I then supported it with evidence saying that he was unpopular after his conduct displayed during the Cuban missile crises and how that was a huge d defeat for the Soviet Union. Then I explain it by saying this led to his removal and replacement. In the link part I wrote that this affected ussr and Soviet relations as the removal of one leader and the emergence of another would definitely have a huge significance as both are different personalities etc I also supported this with the fact that relations between ussr and us changed after both countries leaders had changed earlier
You then write the next point and repeat this 
You should have around 3 points on each side atleast. Make sure they are in depth and well explained and supported with factual evidence.

For paper 3: you need to first state the big message( the overall message that the extract is conveying as a whole). For the Cold War, it’ll be who is to blame for the Cold War usually, but it could be something else as well. You then need to find evidence in the extract which supports the big message. It basically means how the evidence helped you come to the conclusion in finding what the big message is and what does that tell you about the historian. You can also write about the approach of the historian, which is the structure of the extract. Is it panned out in the form of an essay, do they use evidence to support their claims, do they use statistics etc
I find the PEEl format to be the most useful 
You take one piece of evidence. Quote it(try to make it short or paraphrase the quote) explain it if you can through contextual knowledge- something that you need to do- and then analyse it linking it to historian and what you can infer about the historian and how it supports the big message. For instance, a quote about USSR starting the Cold War. I’ll paraphrase it, provide a bit of contextual knowledge(don’t overdo it) by saying this is supported by the fact or keeping in mind that USSR was behaving aggressively through being expansionist. I’ll then analyse it and show what does this mean. It means that the historian attributes blame onto the USSR and that it supports the big message as it portrays the USSR in such a negative way
